title: Building Real Language

examples: Where is the ball? It is under the chair.
Where is mommy? She is in the kitchen.
patterns.goal: asking and answering where things are
saying what you are doing now

patterns.text: What are you doing? I am ___
examples: What are you doing? I am drawing.
What is the bird doing? It is flying.

exits: Child holds a five-turn unrehearsed conversation on a familiar topic.
Child answers wh-questions about a spoken four-sentence story.

activities.title: I spy
activities.how: Describe something in view with one adjective and have the child guess, then let the child give the clue.

activities.title: Hide and find
activities.how: Hide an imagined object in different places and have the child say where it is with Where is ___? It is ___.

activities.title: Shopping list
activities.how: Play a tiny shop where the child asks for items with I have ___ and I would like ___, then swaps to being the shopkeeper.

assessment.ask: Ask where a familiar object is and have the child answer with a full Where is / It is sentence.
Ask what the child has and have them answer with I have ___.
Name an object and have the child describe it with an adjective in a full sentence.
Ask what someone is doing right now and have the child answer with the -ing form.
Ask what the child did yesterday and accept one correct past-tense sentence.
Have the child ask you what you are doing, then answer it together.
Place objects around an imagined scene and have the child use in, on, under, behind.
Have the child give the opposite of four adjective words you say.
Ask the child to read four short words aloud: shop, fish, chip, chair.
Ask the child to read four short words aloud: stop, step, blue, flag.

goals: Name a feeling and connect it to a simple reason.
Show confidence by answering without a hint.
Stay curious when a word is new.
checkin: Ask how the child feels today and have them answer with one feeling word.
Name two feelings and let the child pick which is closer to how they feel today.
Ask what made the child smile today.
praise: You built the whole sentence on your own.
You listened carefully before you answered.
You kept trying after a tricky word.
You found the right word for your idea.
You said it in a full sentence.
You took your time and got it right.
You used a word from an earlier lesson.
encourage: It is fine to think before you answer.
Every mistake teaches us the next step.
You do not have to be fast to be good.

calm.title: Balloon breathing
calm.how: Guide one slow balloon breath: breathe in while lifting the arms, breathe out slowly. Then return to one easy word.

calm.title: Count to five
calm.how: Count slowly to five together, then have the child name one thing that is easy for them to say.

calm.title: Quiet story
calm.how: Tell a three-sentence calm story with no questions, then ask the child to say one word from it.
